data.title: Dropdown
data.tagline: Open a compact menu of actions or destinations
data.description: A dropdown keeps secondary choices behind a trigger when showing them all would add clutter. Name the trigger clearly and keep the menu short and grouped. A frequent or important action should usually remain visible instead of being hidden.

distinctions.label: Select
distinctions.explanation: Dropdown opens actions or navigation. Select chooses and saves a form value.

use: A compact set of related commands
avoid: Hide the main action in a More menu
Put a long, searchable dataset in an action menu
Open the menu from an unlabeled mystery icon
Mix dangerous actions with common choices without separation

lessonPractice.title: Each project row has Rename, Duplicate, and Archive. How do you avoid a row full of buttons?

options.label: Use an inline Dropdown for these related secondary actions, with clear text when opened
options.feedback: Correct. Related secondary commands can share a menu, but should not rely on guessed icons.

options.label: Use three unlabeled icons per row; people will learn them
options.feedback: Icons are often ambiguous, especially for infrequent or risky actions.

options.label: Treat an action as a form value and save it through a Select
options.feedback: These are immediate commands on the current row, not a persistent field value.

data.agentPrompt: Put Rename, Duplicate, and Archive for each project row in a Dropdown with text labels; keep confirmation before Archive. Open and run reversible actions one by one, confirming the menu targets its current row and is fully keyboard-operable.
